title: Route and model tail latency canvas with streaming vs sync comparison
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a production-ready dashboard and supporting pipeline changes that surface p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route, with an explicit breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes. This ticket covers the end-to-end work: metric schema changes and enrichment in the log/metrics pipeline, trace-hook correlation (trace_id -> metric labels), dashboard panels in Grafana/Console, alerting rules for tail regressions, and a plan for sampling and storage cost constraints. Goal: make it easy for SREs, product owners, and on-call to identify model-route combos with degraded tail latency and jump to a representative trace or logs.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50, p95, p99 latency for each model-route pair across selected time ranges
Panels include streaming vs non-streaming split and an aggregated 'tail delta' comparator column
Each latency point links to a sample trace (trace_id) and the corresponding enriched logs for quick RCA
Metrics pipeline emits low-cardinality rollups and a higher-cardinality detail stream for on-demand queries
Alerting rules detect >20% p95 regression on a model-route for a 15m window and create an incident with relevant dashboard link
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Spike completed outlining required metric fields and suggested schema (route, model, io_mode, request_shape).
2026-03-11: Decided to use t-digest histograms for approximate quantiles in metrics backend to reduce storage vs raw pXX series. Documented trade-offs in Confluence.

2026-03-12: Implemented Vector transform prototype to add 'route' and 'model' tags from request metadata and emit a 'latency_ms_hist' histogram metric. PR opened: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/278 (WIP).
2026-03-13: PoC Grafana panels created (internal link). Verified streaming requests are being flagged by io_mode tag. Need sampling plan for traces (1% baseline + 100% for p99 anomalies).
2026-03-14: Integrated trace correlation header (x-rdw-trace) in runtime; backend now stores trace_id in the enriched log event. Working on dashboard drilldown links to trace service.
design_decisions: Use histograms with t-digest aggregation in metrics store rather than storing explicit p50/p95/p99 series for every route-model to control cardinality.
Tag keys: 'route', 'model', 'io_mode' (values: 'streaming'|'sync'), 'shard' (optional for dedicated routing) — keep tags minimal to avoid combinatorial explosion.
Trace sampling: reservoir sample 1% of requests globally; when p95/p99 deviation detected on a route-model, temporarily increase sampling to 100% for 15 minutes for that key.
Log enrichment: add trace_id and request_shape hash at ingestion time so dashboard drilldowns can link directly to logs and traces without backfilling.
Alerting: base alerts on relative regressions (percent delta) and absolute SLO breaches. Use a two-stage alert (warning then critical) to reduce noise.
implementation_notes: Metrics pipeline: add Vector transform to parse request metadata and emit latency_ms_hist histogram. Update schema registry entry 'latency_v2'.
Runtime: include x-rdw-trace header generation and propagation for streaming connectors. Add trace_id to logs emitted by each serving process.
Dashboard: create 'Model-Route Latency Canvas' dashboard with top-left summary table, streaming vs sync split area chart, percentile heatmap, and tail-trace drilldown panel.
Storage: configure rollup job to keep 1s histograms for 2d, 1m rollups for 30d, and 1h rollups for 1y. Coordinate with SRE for retention cost review.
Alerting: add Prometheus/Grafana alert rule templates; add runbook link and escalation path to SRE on-call rotation.
tests: Generate synthetic traffic across 5 models and 8 routes with both streaming and sync modes; verify histograms record expected percentiles within 5% error.
Introduce a synthetic 200ms tail on model 'chat-xl' route '/chat' and assert alert fires within 20 minutes.
Drilldown link from dashboard opens the trace view with matching trace_id and shows the KV cache misses/errors for that request.
Verify cardinality of emitted tag combinations stays within expected budget in staging (<= 10k unique route+model keys).
